messages:
alex: Prometheus alert — remote_write queue saturation in cluster-west. Big spike ~17:42 UTC, dashboards showing scrape bursts across k8s jobs. Filing here so we can triage.
sre-bot: Alert: remote_write_queue_utilization > 90% (job=k8s-pods-west)
maria: saw this on grafana. scrape_samples_sent jumped ~10x for a few minutes. endpoints list also noisy.
jason: Any recent deploys or config changes to kube liveness/readiness that could cause endpoint churn?
alex: ops-oncall rolled a change last night tightening liveness from 20s -> 10s to accelerate restarts for a flaky app. Could be correlated.
maria: that would explain short-lived pods. Prom SD will pick them up and prometheus will attempt scrapes, creating a burst of targets then lots of dropped targets.
jason: logs show repeated lines like:
```
level=warn ts=2025-11-20T17:42:03.123Z caller=manager.go:489 component="scrape manager" msg="target disappeared" job="k8s-pods" target="10.12.3.45:9100" err="target disappeared"
level=error ts=2025-11-20T17:42:04.987Z caller=scrape.go:934 component=scrape target="10.12.3.45:9100" msg="scrape timed out"
```
ops-oncall: quick mitigation options:
- revert the liveness change (we can do a rollback)
- add relabel to avoid scraping pods that aren't Ready or are younger than Xs
- temporary increase remote_write queue capacity while we stabilize
maria: agree. We should also add metric_relabel_configs to drop high-cardinality labels (container_id, request_id, trace_id) from these app metrics so they don't explode TSDB/remote write volume.
alex: Proposed small relabel patch (canary in west prometheus):
```
- job_name: 'k8s-pods'
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: pod
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape]
    regex: "true"
    action: keep
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_ready]
    regex: "true"
    action: keep
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_creation_timestamp]
    regex: "(.+)"
    action: keep
    modulus: 60  # pseudo: ensure pod older than 60s (we'll implement via a small script if prometheus can't do timestamp math)
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - regex: "container_id|request_id|trace_id"
    action: drop
```
(Note: last rule is conceptual—will use appropriate label drop regex)
jason: Also set the job to scrape_interval: 30s and scrape_timeout: 15s to give more breathing room. And add a small random offset to scrape phase on the prometheus side so not all instances align.
ops-oncall: I'll push the relabel/metric_relabel to a canary prometheus in west now. If we see improvement, we can roll to prod and then revert the liveness tweak.
alex: For remote_write queue, temporary config suggestion:
```
remote_write:
- url: https://cortex-write.example/api/prom/push
  queue_config:
    capacity: 5000
    max_shards: 200
    max_samples_per_send: 10000
```
jason: that should reduce immediate backpressure while we fix target churn. After stable, revert queue to safer defaults.
maria: follow-up: create an eval in grafana to track scrape_discarded_targets, scrape_duration_seconds, remote_write_queue_utilization, and metric cardinality for that job for the next 24h.
sre-bot: Incident annotated: root_cause=liveness-probe-change, mitigations=canary_relabel+queue_increase, owner=ops-oncall :warning:
alex: thanks all. Ops will update here with canary results. If canary looks good, we'll 1) roll relabel globally 2) revert liveness change 3) run postmortem and add a playbook for "ephemeral-pod-churn".
ops-oncall: noted, starting canary now. Will post results in 10m. :thumbsup:
